subject.title: Control UI settings pages need one unified design language

question: Should the flat section/group/row anatomy proposed here become the canonical Control UI settings language, and which surfaces should form the first migration phase?
rationale: Source inspection confirms real inconsistency, but code evidence cannot decide whether every listed management page should share one anatomy or which exceptions and rollout sequence maintainers intend.

options.title: Stage a representative pilot
options.body: Define tokens and typed primitives, then migrate Config plus one simpler settings page before approving the broader rollout.

options.title: Adopt across all named surfaces
options.body: Approve the proposed anatomy as mandatory for every listed page and plan a coordinated multi-PR migration.

options.title: Limit to form-like settings
options.body: Standardize only configuration and preference forms while allowing Sessions, Usage, Devices, and hubs to retain purpose-specific layouts.

recommendation.title: Stage a representative pilot
recommendation.body: Define tokens and typed primitives, then migrate Config plus one simpler settings page before approving the broader rollout.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the concrete design direction and are best positioned to confirm the intended product language and scope before implementation ownership is assigned.
